A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same public verification framework for private convex optimization and unlearning. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figure, and appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and several relocations.

before.justification: Section 6, Tables 1–2, and Figure 1 report original EMP-toolkit runtime measurements, scaling analyses, and network simulations for MNIST-scale binary logistic regression.

after.justification: Section 6 retains original verification experiments, revises the network measurements, and adds GPU training-time results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The proposed phased ERM, DP certification, D2D, and Gaussian commitment algorithms retain their objectives and procedures. The D2D training and certification algorithms exchange numbers and locations. The optimizer and step cap described for the new training experiment are experimental implementation choices rather than revisions to the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST-scale binary logistic regression, feature-count and dataset-size sweeps, and the same localhost/LAN/WAN scenarios. Table 3 adds training measurements within this coverage; specifying zero-versus-rest classification does not establish a new task relative to v1's unspecified binary classification.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparison method is added or removed. Shamsabadi et al. (2024), identified as Confidential-DPProof in the references, remains the historical DP-SGD certification comparison; v2 does not introduce a controlled baseline experiment.

E3.justification: The new training experiment uses GPU full-batch gradient descent, a variable learning rate, a 100-step phase limit, and reported privacy parameters adjusted when the target gradient norm is missed. The reported network execution setup changes from v1's virtual-machine description to a Dell/Intel system using Linux traffic control, and communication volume is newly measured. The simulated link speeds and latencies remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds an analysis of whether optimizing the modified ERM creates a practical training bottleneck, accompanied by observations about phase convergence failures. The existing feature-size and dataset-size analyses remain, while the network-overhead analysis receives revised measurements and communication-volume results.

E5.justification: Table 2 changes from point estimates to values with ± uncertainty, although its uncertainty statistic and run count are not explicitly identified. The new training experiment discloses three trials and reports ± values. Table 1's means and standard deviations over three trials are retained; there is no stated increase in runs for those experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces full-verification times of 11.5/11.7/12.8/12.8 hours with 5.54/5.73/6.70/6.88 hours and adds communication volumes; the reported LAN/WAN overheads change from 1.7%/11.4% to 3.4%/24%. These are revised results under a differently described execution setup, not demonstrated same-setting speedups. Table 3 adds training times of 14.37–19.24 seconds. Table 1 and Figure 1 retain their results, including Table 1(c)'s equivalent seconds-to-milliseconds conversion.

T1.justification: The central guarantees and Appendix E proofs are retained after matching renumbered theorems. Limited formal revisions include replacing O-based training-complexity comparisons with Omega-based statements, explicitly allowing aborts in Definition 2.3's honest-curator clause, and correcting the unlearning theorem's description of the interactive protocol. No new central proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal claims about undetectable backdoors and near-optimal DP-SCO with inexpensive certification remain. The introduction adds the empirical claim that training contributes negligibly to end-to-end cost, while Section 4 explicitly extends the efficiency argument to smooth settings through reduced Gaussian commitments.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains public verifiability through trusted public coins and transcript inspection. Section 6 attributes inexpensive training to ordinary GPU computation and discloses convergence failures requiring larger reported epsilon. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit qualification that the historical DP-SGD comparison used 3969 features. The existing convexity and scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the Dell/Intel network-test hardware and Linux traffic-control utility, and newly states that Table 2's full-verification runtimes are estimated from component benchmarks. It also supplies the RTX 2080 training hardware, binary label definition, initial learning rate, learning-rate doubling rule, iteration cap, and privacy-accounting caveat. Existing EMP-toolkit and numerical-precision details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Keinan et al. (2025) on privacy auditing and Menart and Nikolov (2025) on private optimization complexity. The DP-SCO discussion moves from Appendix A to Section 1.1 and gains discussion of high-dimensional tightness and smooth-case comparisons. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 copy-edits the prose, updates author and publication information, moves DP-SCO background and the inference-backdoor construction into the main text, and reorders the utility and certification theorems. It adds an Impact Statement and a public-verifiability appendix. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout with new typography and running headers. Algorithms are extensively reflowed, the D2D certification display moves into the main text, and Figure 1 is resized and relocated. Table 2 gains a communication column and expanded caption, and Table 3 is added.

improvement.justification: Table 3 supplies useful practical training-cost evidence, the experimental documentation becomes more reproducible, and Appendix C clarifies the trust assumptions behind public verification. These provide a limited improvement while the central methods and proofs remain stable. Reporting problems constrain the gain: Table 2's new 2254.7 Mb-per-gradient entry has an unexplained mismatch with 402 ms at 100 Mbit/s, and the historical baseline comparison loses its feature-count qualification.
